chunks: He said: Abul Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad reported to me from his father, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, from Bakr ibn Salih al-Razi, from Sulaiman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, who said:

I heard Abul Hasan, peace be upon him, saying to my father: "How is that I saw you at Abdul Rahman ibn Ya'qub?" He said: "He is my uncle." The Imam said: "He says appalling things about Allah, while Allah cannot be described. Either sit with him and leave us, or sit with us and leave him!" He said: "What is it upon me if I do not say what he says?" The Imam replied: "Do you not fear that a wrath may descend and afflict you all? Do you not know of the companion of Musa whose father was a partisan of Pharaoh? They both drowned. Jibreel said: May Allah have mercy on him, he was not on the belief of his father. But when divine wrath descends, it grants no defense to those near the sinner!"
ai.seo_question: What did the Imam say about associating with those who hold deviant beliefs about God?
ai.summary: Imam Abul Hasan (peace be upon him) admonishes a man for visiting his uncle who held deviant theological views about Allah. Using the parable of Musa's companion who stayed behind to admonish his Pharaoh-supporting father and drowned with him, the Imam teaches that associating with sinners during divine punishment offers no protection, regardless of one's personal innocence. This is a warning about the guilt of association and the dangers of proximity to those who spread theological corruption.
word_analysis: may Allah have mercy on him
